The dance communicates only the distance to food, not its direction.
The angle of the dance is fixed and unrelated to the sun.

questions.explanation: Adjustment after rotation shows the angle carries usable directional information.

distractor_rationales.C: The angle corresponds to direction.
distractor_rationales.B: The bees still found the patch after rotation.
distractor_rationales.D: The angle is measured relative to the sun.

questions.stimulus: Roman fish sauce was made by packing fish with salt and leaving the mixture in the sun for weeks. The salt drew water out of the tissue and suppressed the bacteria that would otherwise spoil it. Amphorae found on shipwrecks still contain residues of the sauce, and their sealed interiors kept the contents from exchanging with seawater.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The sauce survived because seawater flushed through the amphorae.
Salt encouraged the bacteria that spoil fish.
The residues found on shipwrecks are unrelated to fish sauce.
Salt preservation and sealed storage together kept the sauce chemically distinct for centuries.

questions.explanation: Preservation plus sealing explains why residues survived intact.

distractor_rationales.A: Sealed interiors are said to have kept seawater out.
distractor_rationales.B: Salt suppressed spoilage bacteria.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage identifies the residues as the sauce.

questions.stimulus: Deep-sea corals grow in cold water and lack the algae that feed shallow reefs. They capture food from passing currents instead, and their skeletons grow slowly enough that a colony may be centuries old. Radiocarbon dating of a specimen showed that its base was far older than its living branches, so the colony is best understood as a long-lived structure rather than a single animal.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Deep-sea corals depend on algae for food.
The living branches are the oldest part of the colony.
The age of a coral colony is set by the whole structure, not only by its living tissue.
Cold-water corals grow faster than shallow-water corals.

questions.explanation: Dating the base older than the branches shows the structure's age spans the whole colony.

distractor_rationales.D: The passage says their skeletons grow slowly.
distractor_rationales.B: The base is older than the living branches.
distractor_rationales.A: They lack symbiotic algae and catch food from currents.

questions.stimulus: Readers of old books sometimes wrote in the margins. A note may correct a printer's error, argue with the author, or record the date a reader finished the volume. Because marginalia are attached to a specific copy, they can show how one book traveled between owners. Historians therefore treat them as evidence of reading practice rather than as damage to be removed.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: All marginal notes record the same kind of information.
The value of marginalia lies in what they reveal about the people.
Removing marginalia improves the historical record.
Marginalia are valuable mainly because they restore the printed text.

questions.explanation: The notes attach evidence of reading and ownership to a specific copy.

distractor_rationales.D: Their value is evidence of use, not restoration.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage lists several different kinds of note.
distractor_rationales.C: Historians treat the notes as evidence, not damage.

questions.stimulus: A retreating glacier leaves a valley with steep sides and a flat floor. A river valley of similar size usually has a V-shaped cross-section, because running water cuts downward and inward. The U-shape of a glaciated valley therefore records that ice, which erodes sideways as well as downward, once filled the space.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The shape of a valley can indicate whether ice or a river formed it.
Valley shape is unrelated to the agent of erosion.
A retreating glacier leaves a deep V-shaped trench.
Rivers carve U-shaped valleys more often than glaciers do.

questions.explanation: The contrast between U- and V-shaped profiles is the evidence for the erosional agent.

distractor_rationales.D: The text attributes U-shapes to ice and V-shapes to rivers.
distractor_rationales.C: Glacial valleys are described as U-shaped.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage draws the conclusion from shape.

questions.stimulus: Coffee grown under shade trees ripens more slowly than coffee grown in full sun. The slower ripening produces denser beans, and tasters often describe the cup as more complex. Yields per hectare, however, are lower under shade, and farmers must weigh the price premium against the reduced volume harvested.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Shade - grown coffee can earn more per bean.
Shade trees raise yields without affecting quality.
Shade-grown coffee always earns more per hectare than sun-grown coffee.
Full-sun coffee produces denser beans than shade-grown coffee.

questions.explanation: Quality and price rise while volume falls, creating a trade-off.

distractor_rationales.C: The passage says yields are lower, so per-hectare earnings are not guaranteed.
distractor_rationales.D: Slower ripening under shade produces denser beans.
distractor_rationales.B: The text says shade lowers yields.

questions.stimulus: Honey often contains pollen grains from the flowers the bees visited. Because pollen grains have distinctive shapes, a sample can reveal which plants were in bloom. Analysis of a jar from a market stall showed pollen from a plant that flowers only in early spring, several months before the honey was sold. The jar was probably not from the most recent harvest.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Pollen analysis cannot distinguish one season's honey from another's.
Bees visit only one plant species in a season.
The jar was certainly made from artificial honey.
Pollen can date honey by showing which flowering season produced it.

questions.explanation: Season-specific pollen in a jar sold later points to an earlier harvest.

distractor_rationales.A: Distinctive pollen tied to a season is exactly what enables dating.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage infers age, not adulteration.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage describes pollen from visited flowers generally.

questions.stimulus: Shipworms bore into wooden hulls and pilings, digesting the wood with the help of bacteria. A hull recovered from a cold, low-oxygen harbour showed far less damage than one from a warm estuary. Conservators now store excavated timbers in tanks where oxygen is limited, because the animals that attack wood need oxygen as well as wood.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Warm water protects wood from shipworms.
Oxygen has no effect on wood-boring animals.
Limiting oxygen slows the organisms that would otherwise consume waterlogged wood.
Shipworms digest wood without the help of bacteria.

questions.explanation: The comparison and the storage practice both turn on oxygen.

distractor_rationales.A: The warm estuary showed more damage.
distractor_rationales.D: The passage mentions bacterial help.
distractor_rationales.B: The storage method relies on oxygen limitation.

questions.stimulus: A solar still collects drinking water by evaporating brine under a transparent cover and condensing the vapour on the underside. Output depends on sunlight and on the area of the cover. On a cloudy day a small still may produce only a few spoonfuls, while a larger still in full sun produces liters. The device is therefore a supplement rather than a stand-alone supply.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Condensation reduces the amount of water collected.
A solar still's output is too weather-dependent to guarantee water on its own.
A solar still produces the same output in all weather.
Small stills outperform large ones in full sun.

questions.explanation: Variable output under clouds explains why the device is a supplement.

distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes output varying with sunlight and area.
distractor_rationales.D: Larger stills in full sun produce liters.
distractor_rationales.A: Condensation is the collection step.

questions.stimulus: Fish ferment faster in warm weather, and salt slows the process. Communities that live where temperatures stay high use more salt in their preserved fish than communities in cooler regions. A recipe that works in one place can therefore fail in another, not because the method is wrong but because the conditions have changed.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Preservation recipes have to be adjusted to local temperature.
Salt speeds fermentation in warm weather.
Cooler regions require more salt than warmer ones.
A recipe that works in one region always works in another.

questions.explanation: Temperature changes the rate of fermentation, so salt amounts must adapt.

distractor_rationales.B: Salt slows fermentation.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage says warmer communities use more salt.
distractor_rationales.D: The passage says a recipe can fail when conditions change.

questions.stimulus: A cathedral bell is tuned by grinding metal from its rim. Removing material lowers the pitch and can also change the relationships among the bell's partial tones. Founders therefore remove metal in small stages, testing between each. A bell ground too far cannot be restored, because the metal cannot be added back.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Tuning is irreversible, so it proceeds cautiously and in measured steps.
Grinding raises the pitch of a bell.
Partial tones are unaffected by removing metal.
Founders grind the rim quickly because extra metal can be added later.

questions.explanation: Irreversibility explains the incremental method. The keyed choice follows from the passage's stated relationship, while the other options either contradict it or go beyond what the text supports.

distractor_rationales.D: Metal cannot be added back.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage says removing material lowers pitch.
distractor_rationales.C: Grinding can change the partial relationships.

questions.stimulus: Compacted soil resists root growth even when it holds enough water. Roots follow pores and cracks, and compaction closes those channels. In a field where machinery has passed repeatedly, roots may spread sideways above a hard layer instead of reaching deeper moisture. The plants survive but depend on rain in the upper soil.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Compaction makes crops more vulnerable to drought in the upper soil.
Roots grow through compacted soil more easily than through pores.
Machinery traffic improves the soil's pore structure.
Compaction helps roots reach deeper water.

questions.explanation: The passage links shallow roots to reliance on upper-soil moisture, so drought there is the logical risk.

distractor_rationales.D: Roots are blocked from deeper layers.
distractor_rationales.B: Roots follow pores, which compaction closes.
distractor_rationales.C: Traffic is the cause of the compaction described.

questions.stimulus: Soot deposits on cave ceilings accumulate in thin layers that record the fires below. A layer rich in charcoal indicates a larger or more frequent fire; a gap indicates a period without burning. Archaeologists reading a sequence of layers can therefore reconstruct how often people used a cave, even when no tools survive.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Soot layers form only when a cave is empty of people.
Soot layers provide a record of human activity independent of artefacts.
Charcoal-rich layers indicate cold weather rather than fires.
A gap in the layers proves that the cave was never visited.

questions.explanation: The layers record burning even when no tools survive, which is why they can establish occupation independently.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage says the layers record use.
distractor_rationales.D: A gap indicates a period without burning, not no visits.
distractor_rationales.C: Charcoal richness tracks fire size or frequency.

questions.stimulus: Harbour sediment traps lead, copper and organic matter washed from streets and ships. A core taken near a former shipyard contains a sharp peak in copper at the depth corresponding to the yard's busiest decades. Above that layer, concentrations fall as the yard closed and runoff was diverted. The core therefore reads as a history of industrial activity.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Chemical layers in harbour mud can be tied to the rise and fall of nearby industry.
Copper concentrations rise after the shipyard closed.
Harbour sediment carries no trace of industrial activity.
The peak in copper came from natural erosion only.

questions.explanation: The copper peak aligns with the shipyard's busiest years, so the sediment layers track the industry's rise and fall.

distractor_rationales.B: Concentrations fall above the peak as the yard closed.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes clear traces.
distractor_rationales.D: The peak corresponds to the yard's busiest decades.

questions.stimulus: Bats that hibernate through winter need high humidity as well as steady cold. Dry air draws water from their skin and wings, and an aroused bat burns fat it cannot replace until spring. A cave that is cold but draughty can therefore be worse for a colony than one that is slightly warmer but still.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Bats can replace fat easily during winter.
Air movement has no effect on hibernating bats.
Stable, humid conditions matter more to hibernating bats than cold alone.
Warm, dry caves are ideal for hibernating bats.

questions.explanation: Humidity and stillness protect the fat reserve that must last the winter.

distractor_rationales.D: Dry air causes water loss and arousal.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage says fat cannot be replaced until spring.
distractor_rationales.B: Draughty caves are described as harmful.

questions.stimulus: Roof tiles are laid so that each row overlaps the one below. Water running down the slope crosses from one tile to the next without reaching the deck beneath. If the overlap is too small, wind-driven rain can be forced upward under the edge. The overlap is therefore a specification, not a decorative choice.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Overlap width must be set to withstand the weather.
The overlap has no effect on whether rain reaches the deck.
Water runs upward across the roof under normal conditions.
A smaller overlap gives better protection in strong wind.

questions.explanation: Because wind-driven rain can enter under a small overlap, the overlap must be sized for the weather the roof will face.

distractor_rationales.D: Too small an overlap lets wind-driven rain under the edge.
distractor_rationales.C: Water runs down the slope; only driven rain moves upward.
distractor_rationales.B: The overlap determines whether water crosses safely.

questions.stimulus: Some plants rely on ants to carry their seeds. The seed carries a fleshy appendage that ants eat, and the seed itself is discarded underground. Seeds moved this way end up buried, where they escape drying and some seed-eaters. The plant pays a small food cost for dispersal and burial.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Seeds left on the surface survive better than buried ones.
The food reward buys the seed both transport and a safer place to germinate.
Ants destroy the seeds they carry.
The appendage prevents ants from moving the seed.

questions.explanation: Transport plus burial explains the benefit of the food cost.

distractor_rationales.C: The seed is discarded intact underground.
distractor_rationales.D: The appendage is the reward that attracts ants.
distractor_rationales.A: Burial is described as protection.

questions.stimulus: Clipper ships carried tea from China to London, and speed mattered because early arrivals sold at higher prices. Their hulls were narrow and their sail area large, which made them fast in strong winds but hard to handle in a calm. After steamships offered reliable schedules, the clippers lost their advantage.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Reliability of arrival proved more valuable than the fastest possible passage.
Clippers remained the fastest option after steamships appeared.
Speed had no effect on the price tea fetched.
Calm weather was the clippers' greatest advantage.

questions.explanation: Steam's dependable schedule displaced the clipper's speed premium.

distractor_rationales.B: Clippers lost their advantage to steamships.
distractor_rationales.D: The narrow hull was hard to handle in a calm.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage says early arrivals sold higher.

questions.stimulus: Some birds lay eggs with thinner shells where the soil is low in calcium. The birds cannot manufacture calcium, so they must take it from food or grit. Studies of a population on calcium-poor ground found thinner shells and more breakages than in a population on limestone. The difference tracked geology, not species.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Birds can synthesise calcium without eating it.
Access to calcium in the environment shapes shell thickness in these birds.
Shell thickness is fixed by the species and cannot vary.

questions.explanation: The geologic contrast, with the same species, isolates calcium availability.

distractor_rationales.D: The two populations differ within the same species.
distractor_rationales.B: Thin shells occur on poor ground.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage says birds must obtain calcium from food or grit.

questions.stimulus: Residue inside Roman amphorae can be identified by its chemical signature. Jars found in a storage room contained traces of olive oil, while jars from a nearby shop contained fish sauce. The two sets were the same shape. Shape alone therefore does not tell an archaeologist what a vessel carried.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Fish sauce and olive oil leave identical residues.
Contents must be identified chemically, because form does not reveal use.
All jars in a storage room held the same product.
Amphora shape reliably indicates what was stored inside.

questions.explanation: Same shape, different contents forces chemical identification. The keyed choice follows from the passage's stated relationship, while the other options either contradict it or go beyond what the text supports.

distractor_rationales.D: Identical shapes held different contents.
distractor_rationales.A: The distinction comes from chemical signatures.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage contrasts two nearby sets.

questions.stimulus: Pencil leads are graded by hardness, which depends on the ratio of graphite to clay. More clay makes a harder lead that holds a sharp point and prints lightly; more graphite makes a softer lead that darkens the page and wears quickly. A drafter choosing a lead is choosing between precision and darkness.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The graphite-to-clay ratio has no effect on wear.
Hard leads darken the page more than soft leads.
No single lead suits both fine detail and dense shading equally well.
Clay increases the darkness of a pencil line.

questions.explanation: The trade-off between point retention and darkness is the basis of the grading scale.

distractor_rationales.B: Hard leads print lightly; soft leads darken.
distractor_rationales.D: Graphite provides darkness, not clay.
distractor_rationales.A: The ratio determines both darkness and wear.

questions.stimulus: A bleached coral reef can recover if the algae that live inside the coral return while the coral is still alive. Recovery is slower where the reef is also stressed by sediment or warm water. Surveys find that reefs with cleaner water regain color sooner after a bleaching event than reefs near river mouths.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Bleached coral is always dead and cannot recover.
Sediment speeds the return of algae to coral.
Warm water improves recovery after bleaching.
Reducing local stress helps a reef recover from bleaching.

questions.explanation: The comparison points to local stress as a brake on recovery.

distractor_rationales.B: Cleaner-water reefs recovered sooner.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage describes recovery while the coral is alive.
distractor_rationales.C: Warm water is named as an additional stress.

questions.stimulus: Salmon that die after spawning leave carcasses in streams. Their bodies carry nitrogen from the ocean, which enters the food web as the carcasses decay. Trees along a stream with many spawning salmon contain more marine-derived nitrogen than trees along a stream without them. The forest is therefore linked to the ocean by the fish.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Marine nutrients reach streamside forests through the bodies of spawning fish.
Trees cannot take up nitrogen from decaying fish.
Salmon remove nitrogen from streamside forests.
The connection exists only in streams without spawning salmon.

questions.explanation: The nitrogen signature in trees traces the marine source through the carcasses.

distractor_rationales.B: The passage reports elevated nitrogen in those trees.
distractor_rationales.C: The carcasses add nitrogen.
distractor_rationales.D: The contrast is between streams with and without salmon.

questions.stimulus: A windmill's sails turn a shaft, and gearing converts that slow, powerful rotation into a faster one at the millstone. Changing the gear ratio changes the speed of the stone without changing the wind. Millers keep several gears on hand so that a strong wind and a light one can both be used.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Gearing lets a miller match the stone's speed to the available wind.
A single fixed gear ratio suits every wind condition.
The millstone turns more slowly than the shaft in all gears.
Gearing changes the amount of wind reaching the sails.

questions.explanation: Multiple gears exist to keep stone speed steady across wind strengths.

distractor_rationales.D: Gearing converts rotation, not wind.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage describes changing ratios for different winds.
distractor_rationales.C: The gearing speeds the rotation up at the stone.

questions.stimulus: A manuscript written with acidic ink can lose text at the same time it loses paper. Washing a leaf removes acid but may also lift the ink, so conservators first test a small, unimportant area. If the ink survives the test, the leaf can be washed; if not, it is stored dry and digitised instead.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Every leaf can be washed safely with acidic ink.
Testing a small area damages the whole manuscript.
Digitisation removes acid from the paper.
Treatment decisions depend on evidence from a test before the whole leaf is exposed.

questions.explanation: The small-area test governs whether the full treatment is safe.

distractor_rationales.A: Washing may lift the ink.
distractor_rationales.B: The test uses an unimportant area precisely to avoid damage.
distractor_rationales.C: Digitisation creates a copy; it does not treat the paper.

questions.stimulus: Moss on a stone wall is thickest on the side that receives the most moisture, not always the side that receives the most light. On a wall shaded by trees, moss may cover the whole face, while an exposed wall carries moss in a band near the ground. Anyone reading moss as a compass would need to know the local conditions.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Moss requires full sunlight and avoids damp surfaces.
Moss always grows on the north side of a wall regardless of shade.
A shaded wall carries less moss than an exposed one.
Moss growth reflects moisture and shade, so it is an unreliable direction indicator without local context.

questions.explanation: Moisture and shade dominate, which defeats naive compass use.

distractor_rationales.B: The passage says moisture matters more than direction.
distractor_rationales.A: Moss is thickest where moisture is greatest.
distractor_rationales.C: The shaded wall may be covered entirely.

questions.stimulus: Volcanic lightning occurs in ash clouds when particles collide and separate charge. The effect is more common in eruptions that produce fine ash and vigorous convection. Observers have used lightning detection to track eruptions at night and in bad weather, when cameras see little. The electrical signal becomes a remote sensing tool.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Volcanic lightning occurs only in eruptions with no ash.
Cameras see eruptions better at night than detectors do.
Lightning detection replaces the need to monitor volcanoes.
Detecting lightning can reveal an eruption that visibility would hide.

questions.explanation: The electrical signal works when visual observation fails.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage ties lightning to fine ash and convection.
distractor_rationales.C: It is a tool, not a replacement for monitoring.
distractor_rationales.B: The text says cameras see little at night and in bad weather.

questions.stimulus: Wool takes dye unevenly if its scales are damaged. Makers therefore clean fleece gently and avoid sudden temperature changes during dyeing, since a rapid shift can shock the fibres. A dye lot that looks patchy often records a handling error rather than a fault in the dye itself.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Rapid temperature changes improve the evenness of dye uptake.
Damaged scales help wool absorb dye uniformly.
Even color depends on gentle handling as much as on the dye recipe.
Patchiness always indicates a faulty dye.

questions.explanation: Handling errors, not the dye, explain many patchy lots.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage warns that rapid shifts shock the fibres.
distractor_rationales.B: Damage is described as causing uneven uptake.
distractor_rationales.D: Patchiness often reflects handling, not the dye.

questions.stimulus: Charcoal in lake sediment comes from fires in the surrounding catchment. A layer with abundant charcoal often coincides with a shift from forest pollen to grass pollen. The two signals together suggest that fire removed trees and allowed grasses to spread. Neither signal alone would establish the sequence.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Charcoal layers indicate that no fire occurred in the catchment.
Combining charcoal and pollen evidence links fire to vegetation change.
Pollen shifts always precede fires by several centuries.
Grass pollen excludes the possibility of fire.

questions.explanation: The coincidence of the two proxies is what ties fire to the vegetation shift.

distractor_rationales.A: Charcoal records fire.
distractor_rationales.C: The signals are described as coinciding.
distractor_rationales.D: Grass pollen follows fire in the proposed sequence.

questions.stimulus: A tea clipper's narrow hull reduced drag but also reduced cargo space. Owners packed light, high-value cargo such as tea and raced for the first market. When the Suez Canal opened, steamships could take a shorter route that sailing ships could not use reliably. The clippers' advantage narrowed.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: A route change reduced the value of the clippers' speed and small capacity.
Clippers carried bulk cargo more cheaply after the canal opened.
The Suez Canal made the clippers' route shorter than the steamships'.

questions.explanation: The canal favored steam, eroding the clipper's niche.

distractor_rationales.D: Steamships took the shorter route the clippers could not use.
distractor_rationales.C: Clippers carried light, high-value cargo.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage says the narrow hull reduced capacity.

questions.stimulus: A bell foundry casts a bell slightly larger than its final size because tuning removes metal. The founder also adjusts the profile so that the bell's partial tones form the intended chord. Changing the profile after casting is nearly impossible, so the shape must be right before the metal cools.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Tuning adds metal to raise the pitch.
The partial tones are unrelated to the bell's shape.
A bell's profile can be reshaped easily after casting.
Most of a bell's tonal character is fixed at casting, with tuning only refining it.

questions.explanation: Since profile cannot be changed later, the cast shape carries the tonal design.

distractor_rationales.C: The passage says reshaping after casting is nearly impossible.
distractor_rationales.A: Tuning removes metal.
distractor_rationales.B: The profile is adjusted to shape the partials.

questions.stimulus: An oyster reef filters water as its inhabitants feed. A dense reef can clear suspended particles from a large volume in a day. When reefs were removed, water clarity fell and sunlight reached less deeply. Seagrasses, which need light, declined in the same estuaries.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Water clarity improved after reefs were removed.
Oyster reefs increase suspended particles in the water.
Losing oyster reefs can reduce water clarity enough to harm seagrass.
Seagrasses grow better in turbid water.

questions.explanation: Filtration loss, lower clarity and seagrass decline form the causal chain.

distractor_rationales.B: The reef filters particles out.
distractor_rationales.D: Seagrass needs light, which turbidity blocks.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage says clarity fell.

questions.stimulus: A mudbrick wall shrinks as it dries. If the outer surface dries faster than the core, the difference in shrinkage pulls the surface apart. Builders therefore mix straw into the clay, which slows drying and gives the shrinking mass something to hold onto. The cracks that appear in unstrawed brick begin at the surface.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Mudbrick does not change size as it dries.
Straw reduces cracking by evening out the drying of a mudbrick.
Straw speeds drying and increases surface shrinkage.
Cracks in unstrawed brick start at the core.

questions.explanation: Straw moderates the moisture gradient that causes surface cracking.

distractor_rationales.C: The passage says straw slows drying.
distractor_rationales.A: The wall shrinks as it dries.
distractor_rationales.D: The text says cracks begin at the surface.

questions.stimulus: Goats browse young trees before they can grow above reach. On islands where goats were removed, tree lines moved upslope within decades. On islands where goats remained, the same species stayed low and sparse. The difference between the islands tracks the presence of goats rather than climate.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Goats help young trees grow above browsing height.
Removing goats prevented trees from spreading.
Grazing animals can hold a tree line in place.
Tree lines are determined entirely by temperature.

questions.explanation: The island comparison isolates grazing as the cause.

distractor_rationales.D: The paired islands share climate but differ in goats.
distractor_rationales.B: Tree lines moved upslope after removal.
distractor_rationales.A: Goats browse young trees before they escape reach.

questions.stimulus: Lichens absorb water and nutrients directly through their surfaces, which also means they absorb pollutants. A lichen transplanted from a clean site to a city center accumulates metals within months. Species differ in tolerance, so a survey of which lichens survive can map pollution without instruments.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Lichens filter out pollutants and remain unaffected.
Lichen communities can act as biological pollution monitors.
All lichen species respond to pollution in the same way.

questions.explanation: Absorption plus species-specific tolerance supports biomonitoring. The keyed choice follows from the passage's stated relationship, while the other options either contradict it or go beyond what the text supports.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage says they absorb pollutants.
distractor_rationales.C: Tolerance differs by species.
distractor_rationales.D: The transplant accumulated metals within months.

questions.stimulus: Dredging records show how often a harbour was cleared. Sediment cores show layers of coarse material where dredging mixed the bed. Where the two records agree, historians can date a period of increased shipping. Where they disagree, one source is probably incomplete.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Disagreement proves both records are correct.
Agreement between independent records strengthens a claim about harbour use.
Dredging records and sediment cores always agree.
Coarse sediment indicates that no dredging occurred.

questions.explanation: Cross-checking two independent records is what supports the dating.

distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes cases where they disagree.
distractor_rationales.D: Mixed beds leave coarse layers.
distractor_rationales.A: Disagreement is explained as incompleteness in one source.

questions.stimulus: In permafrost, ice wedges form when meltwater enters cracks and refreezes. Repeated widening pushes the surrounding ground upward and outward, creating patterned polygons at the surface. Where the climate warms, wedges melt and the polygons subside. The pattern is therefore a visible record of ground temperature.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The patterns are unrelated to temperature.
Melting ice wedges raises the ground surface.
Changing polygon patterns can signal thawing permafrost.
Polygons form only where the ground never freezes.

questions.explanation: The surface pattern tracks the state of the ice wedges.

distractor_rationales.D: Freezing meltwater is the mechanism.
distractor_rationales.B: Melting causes subsidence.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage links the pattern to ground temperature.

questions.stimulus: A fresco is painted on wet lime plaster. As the plaster sets, the pigment becomes part of the wall, which is why the color lasts. The painter must work quickly, because once the plaster dries the surface will not accept pigment in the same way. Frescoes were therefore planned in sections sized to one day's work.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: A painter could return to the same section weeks later.
The technique's durability depends on painting before the plaster sets.
Fresco pigment sits on top of dry plaster.
The sections were sized to the painter's arm length only.

questions.explanation: The wet-plaster window explains both durability and the daily section plan.

distractor_rationales.C: The pigment becomes part of the wall as it sets.
distractor_rationales.A: Dry plaster will not accept pigment the same way.
distractor_rationales.D: Sections matched a day's work, not arm length.

questions.stimulus: A bridge cable is protected from rust by a galvanised coating that corrodes before the steel beneath. The coating is sacrificial: it gives up metal so the cable does not. Once the coating is consumed, the steel begins to rust, so inspectors measure coating thickness rather than waiting for visible damage.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Inspectors should ignore the coating and wait for rust.
Measuring the protective layer gives earlier warning than looking for rust.
Galvanising makes steel immune to corrosion.
The coating outlasts the steel it protects.

questions.explanation: Coating thickness is an early indicator of remaining protection.

distractor_rationales.C: The coating corrodes so the steel does not.
distractor_rationales.A: By the time rust shows, the coating is gone.
distractor_rationales.D: Once consumed, the steel begins to rust.

questions.stimulus: A fish's otolith grows in annual rings, much like a tree. The rings record the temperature and chemistry of the water the fish inhabited, and a single otolith carries the whole life history of one animal. Researchers can therefore place a fish in particular waters at particular ages, even after it has been caught far away.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: An otolith changes after the fish dies, erasing its history.
Otoliths preserve a dated record of the environments.
Otolith rings record only the fish's age, not its environment.

questions.explanation: Annual layers with environmental chemistry allow life-history reconstruction.

distractor_rationales.D: The rings record water chemistry as well as age.
distractor_rationales.A: The record survives in the recovered ear stone.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes annual rings.

questions.stimulus: In stony deserts, stones sometimes sit on pedestals of fine soil. Wind removes the loose material around a stone but cannot lift the stone itself, so the ground beneath it erodes more slowly. Over time the stone appears to rise. The pedestal is therefore a record of wind erosion, not of the stone being pushed upward.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The stone is gradually lifted by rising air currents.
Pedestals form only where the ground is fully protected from wind.
The surrounding ground has been lowered, leaving the stone elevated.
Wind deposits soil beneath the stone.

questions.explanation: Wind removes the surrounding soil faster than the protected ground beneath the stone, so the stone appears to rise.

distractor_rationales.A: Deflation removes material around the stone.
distractor_rationales.D: The pedestal remains because erosion is slower beneath the stone.
distractor_rationales.B: Wind erosion is the mechanism, not protection.

questions.stimulus: Many mushrooms fruit after rain, but rain alone is not enough. The mycelium must already have stored enough nutrients, and the air must cool enough to trigger development. A dry summer followed by a single storm often produces no flush, while a wet autumn with mild nights produces a large one.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: A single storm is sufficient to produce a mushroom flush.
Mycelium stores no nutrients before fruiting.
Mushrooms fruit best in dry, warm conditions.
Fruiting depends on accumulated reserves and temperature as well as moisture.

questions.explanation: The passage identifies stored nutrients, cool nights and moisture as joint requirements, so no single storm is sufficient.

distractor_rationales.A: The passage says rain alone is not enough.
distractor_rationales.C: Cooling nights and wet weather favor fruiting.
distractor_rationales.B: Reserves are described as necessary.

questions.stimulus: People often assume that a desert is empty of life because it looks bare. A closer look at a single square meter of sand can reveal seeds, dormant eggs and buried insects waiting for rain. Within days of a storm, the same ground may be covered with seedlings and insects that were invisible before.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares two deserts and concludes that they are identical.
It states a common assumption and then presents evidence.
It lists several causes and ranks them by importance.
It describes a process step by step from beginning to end.

questions.explanation: The passage opens with an assumption, then offers hidden life as the correction.

distractor_rationales.C: There is no ranking of causes.
distractor_rationales.D: No sequential process is described.
distractor_rationales.A: Only one setting is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A hand loom and a power loom produce the same cloth, but they organize work differently. On a hand loom the weaver controls pace and pattern at every pass. A power loom fixes the pace and moves pattern control into the punch card or the computer. The change is less about speed than about where decisions sit.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To explain how mechanisation shifted control over pattern and pace away from the weaver.
To describe the technical steps of warping a loom.
To show that power looms produce no patterned cloth.
To argue that hand-woven cloth is of better quality.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts two looms and locates the real change in decision-making.

distractor_rationales.D: Quality is not compared.
distractor_rationales.B: Warping is never mentioned.
distractor_rationales.C: Pattern control is relocated, not eliminated.

questions.stimulus: Early maps of the ocean floor were assembled from lead lines dropped over the side. Each sounding gave one depth at one point. A century later, sonar surveyed whole swaths in a single pass. The difference is not merely accuracy: it is the shift from a scatter of points to a continuous surface.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that early maps were more accurate than sonar maps.
It contrasts two surveying methods and explains what the change made possible.
It narrates a single voyage in chronological order.
It lists the materials used to build sounding lines.

questions.explanation: The passage juxtaposes lead-line and sonar surveys and names the conceptual gain.

distractor_rationales.C: No voyage is described.
distractor_rationales.D: Materials are not listed.
distractor_rationales.A: Sonar is presented as the advance.

questions.stimulus: A paper conservator faced with a brittle volume has two options. Washing removes acid but risks the ink. Deacidification spray neutralises acid with less moisture but penetrates unevenly. The choice depends on the ink, the paper and how much time the collection can spare.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It explains why brittle paper cannot be treated at all.
It presents two options, notes the risk of each, and says the choice is conditional.
It describes the history of paper manufacture in order.
It recommends one treatment as correct in every case.

questions.explanation: Two treatments, their risks, and conditional advice structure the passage.

distractor_rationales.D: The passage says the choice is conditional.
distractor_rationales.C: No manufacturing history is given.
distractor_rationales.A: Treatments are offered, not ruled out.

questions.stimulus: Bamboo is often called a grass, and the label matters. It grows from an underground rhizome, sends up hollow stems, and dies back after flowering. Each of these traits is shared with grasses and not with the trees it resembles. The resemblance to wood is a matter of size, not of family.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To describe how bamboo is harvested and dried.
To explain why bamboo's botanical traits place it with grasses rather than trees.
To compare the strength of bamboo and steel.
To argue that bamboo should be classified as a hardwood.

questions.explanation: Shared grass traits are the evidence behind the classification. The keyed choice matches the passage's actual movement and purpose, while the other options describe content or functions the text does not contain.

distractor_rationales.D: The passage separates bamboo from trees.
distractor_rationales.A: Harvesting is not discussed.
distractor_rationales.C: No strength comparison appears.

questions.stimulus: A new bridge design was tested in a wind tunnel at increasing speeds. At low speeds the deck behaved as predicted. At a critical speed the deck began to twist, and the twisting grew instead of settling. The test was stopped, and the section was reshaped before the next run.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares two bridge designs and declares one superior.
It explains the theory of wind loading without describing a test.
It lists several failures from different laboratories.
It narrates a test in sequence and ends with the response to a failure.

questions.explanation: The passage follows the test from low speed to failure to redesign.

distractor_rationales.A: Only one design is tested.
distractor_rationales.B: A concrete test is described.
distractor_rationales.C: There is a single test sequence.

questions.stimulus: Salt marshes absorb wave energy, store carbon and shelter young fish. They also migrate inland as sea level rises, but only if the land behind them is open. Where a seawall blocks that retreat, the marsh is squeezed against a hard edge and drowns. Protection therefore depends on what lies behind the marsh.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes the formation of salt marshes from bare mud.
It argues that seawalls are the best way to protect marshes.
It lists benefits, introduces a condition for survival, and draws a conclusion about that condition.
It compares marshes in two countries and finds no difference.

questions.explanation: Benefits, a migration condition, and the blocking seawall build to the conclusion.

distractor_rationales.A: Formation from mud is not described.
distractor_rationales.B: Seawalls are the obstacle in the example.
distractor_rationales.D: No country comparison appears.

questions.stimulus: The claim that goldfish have three-second memories is repeated so often that it has become a fact in popular telling. Experiments with trained fish show them returning to a feeding site weeks later. The repetition of the claim, not the evidence, explains its persistence.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To confirm that goldfish memory lasts only seconds.
To challenge a widely repeated claim by pointing to contrary evidence.
To explain how to train a goldfish to feed on cue.
To describe the anatomy of the goldfish brain.

questions.explanation: The passage sets a popular claim against experimental evidence and explains its persistence.

distractor_rationales.C: Training is mentioned as evidence, not as instruction.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage contradicts the three-second claim.
distractor_rationales.D: Anatomy is never discussed.

questions.stimulus: A weaver preparing a warp winds hundreds of threads onto a beam, keeping each at even tension. If one thread is tighter, it pulls the cloth out of shape later. The preparation is slow and invisible in the finished fabric, which is why it is easy to skimp and expensive to get wrong.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To compare two kinds of loom in detail.
To describe the visible pattern of a finished cloth.
To explain why an invisible preparatory step matters to the final product.
To argue that warp preparation can safely be skipped.

questions.explanation: The passage connects an unseen preparation to a visible consequence.

distractor_rationales.B: The step's invisibility is the point.
distractor_rationales.D: Skimping is described as costly.
distractor_rationales.A: Looms are not compared here.

questions.stimulus: Some seeds remain dormant for decades even when conditions seem right. Scarification, whether by heat, abrasion or passage through an animal, can break that dormancy. The seed is not waiting passively; it is holding a lock that only particular events can open.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes an observation, illustrates it with examples, and closes with a comparison.
It argues that dormancy is simply a passive waiting period.
It lists the chemical steps of germination in order.
It presents a chronological history of seed science.

questions.explanation: Observation, examples, then the lock metaphor shape the passage.

distractor_rationales.D: No historical sequence is offered.
distractor_rationales.B: The final sentence rejects pure passivity.
distractor_rationales.C: Chemical steps are not given.

questions.stimulus: An acoustic engineer testing a lecture hall found that speech was clear in the front rows but muddled at the back. The ceiling reflected sound back to the front while the rear received echoes from a flat wall. Adding curved diffusers at the rear changed the pattern without adding amplification.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that amplification is the only solution.
It compares two halls and finds both equally clear.
It describes a problem, identifies its cause, and reports a solution.
It lists materials used in hall construction.

questions.explanation: Problem, cause and remedy structure the paragraph. The keyed choice matches the passage's actual movement and purpose, while the other options describe content or functions the text does not contain.

distractor_rationales.B: Only one hall is discussed.
distractor_rationales.D: Materials are incidental.
distractor_rationales.A: The solution avoids amplification.

questions.stimulus: A river that once meandered across a floodplain was straightened for navigation. The shortened channel carried water away faster, which deepened the bed and lowered the water table beside it. Farmland that had relied on the high water table dried, and the river began to cut downward rather than spread sideways.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It traces a chain of consequences that followed a single alteration.
It argues that straightening a river has no downstream effects.
It describes the construction of a navigation lock.
It compares two rivers and ranks their water quality.

questions.explanation: The paragraph moves from straightening to deepening to a lowered water table and dried farmland.

distractor_rationales.D: One river is followed.
distractor_rationales.C: No lock construction is described.
distractor_rationales.B: Consequences are the subject of the passage.

questions.stimulus: A museum label once told visitors that a wooden mask was used in ceremonies. No record supported the claim. When the catalog was revised, the label was replaced with a note that the mask's use is unknown and that the wood dates to the twelfth century. The absence of evidence became part of the display.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To prove that the mask was used in ceremonies.
To show how acknowledging missing evidence can improve an exhibit.
To describe the carving techniques used on the mask.
To explain how wooden objects are dated by museums.

questions.explanation: The revision turns an unsupported claim into an honest label.

distractor_rationales.C: Carving is not described.
distractor_rationales.A: The passage says the ceremony claim lacked support.
distractor_rationales.D: Dating is mentioned but not explained.

questions.stimulus: Two methods exist for measuring a forest's carbon. One counts every tree in sample plots and estimates the rest. The other uses laser scanning from an aircraft to map canopy height. Plot counts are accurate but slow; scanning is fast but needs calibration against plots. Neither stands alone.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that forest carbon cannot be measured.
It describes a single method in step-by-step detail.
It compares two methods, names the limits of each, and concludes that they depend on one another.
It recommends abandoning plot counts in favor of scanning.

questions.explanation: The contrast and the calibration requirement produce the joint conclusion.

distractor_rationales.D: Plot counts are needed for calibration.
distractor_rationales.B: Two methods are compared.
distractor_rationales.A: Measurement is described as possible.

questions.stimulus: A bell is rung once and the sound continues for many seconds. A listener hears a fundamental note plus weaker tones above it. The shape of the bell determines which of those tones are strong, and shifting one part of the profile can make a bell sound bright or dull without changing its fundamental pitch.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To describe the metal alloy used in bell casting.
To explain how a bell's shape shapes its tone beyond the fundamental note.
To argue that a bell produces only one tone.
To explain how bell ringers time their strokes.

questions.explanation: The passage links profile shape to the strength of upper tones.

distractor_rationales.A: Alloy is not mentioned.
distractor_rationales.C: The passage describes multiple tones.
distractor_rationales.D: Ringing technique is not discussed.

questions.stimulus: Coastal dunes form when wind carries sand inland until vegetation slows it. The plants trap grains, and the dune grows upward. A single storm can cut the dune back, but the roots usually survive. The dune is therefore built slowly and destroyed quickly, a pattern that shapes how coastlines are managed.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It explains a formation process, notes a countervailing force, and draws a management implication.
It argues that storms build dunes faster than vegetation does.
It lists the plant species found on dunes.
It tells the history of one particular coastline.

questions.explanation: Growth, storm damage and management follow one another. The keyed choice matches the passage's actual movement and purpose, while the other options describe content or functions the text does not contain.

distractor_rationales.D: No specific coastline is followed.
distractor_rationales.B: Storms cut dunes back.
distractor_rationales.C: Species are not listed.

questions.stimulus: Every year the same lake freezes later than it did a century ago. Records kept by a monastery note the first day of ice each winter. The series is not continuous, but the trend survives the gaps. A record kept for another purpose has become evidence for a changing climate.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To compare two lakes and explain their differences.
To describe the physics of lake freezing in detail.
To argue that the monastery records are useless.
To show how an incidental historical record can document long-term change.

questions.explanation: The final sentence states the reinterpretation of an old record.

distractor_rationales.B: The physics is not the subject.
distractor_rationales.C: The records are presented as valuable.
distractor_rationales.A: Only one lake is discussed.

questions.stimulus: A chef testing a new oven found that the same recipe produced different results on different shelves. The top shelf browned too quickly, the bottom stayed pale. The chef rotated the trays halfway through and the variation fell. The oven's heat was uneven, and the method had been hiding it.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that oven shelves make no difference.
It lists the ingredients of the recipe.
It compares two ovens made by different manufacturers.
It reports observations, describes a fix, and explains what the observations revealed.

questions.explanation: Observation, remedy and diagnosis form the sequence. The keyed choice matches the passage's actual movement and purpose, while the other options describe content or functions the text does not contain.

distractor_rationales.A: Shelf position is the variable.
distractor_rationales.B: Ingredients are not listed.
distractor_rationales.C: One oven is tested.

questions.stimulus: Some desert plants open their pores at night rather than during the day. The cooler air reduces water loss, and the plant stores the carbon it takes in until daylight. The strategy trades a slower process for a much smaller water bill, which matters where rain is rare.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To compare desert plants with rainforest species.
To explain how a night-time strategy reduces water loss in dry conditions.
To argue that opening pores at midday is more efficient.
To describe how desert plants store water in their leaves.

questions.explanation: The passage links timing, temperature and water loss. The keyed choice matches the passage's actual movement and purpose, while the other options describe content or functions the text does not contain.

distractor_rationales.D: Storage of water is not described.
distractor_rationales.C: Midday opening would increase loss.
distractor_rationales.A: No rainforest comparison appears.

questions.stimulus: A clockmaker adjusts a pendulum's length to change its period. A longer pendulum swings more slowly; a shorter one swings faster. Temperature matters too, because metal expands in warmth. Precision clocks therefore use alloys that change little with heat, or compensate with a second metal that expands in the opposite direction.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It states a basic relationship, introduces a complication, and describes two responses to it.
It argues that temperature has no effect on clocks.
It narrates the invention of the pendulum clock.
It lists the parts of a clock in the order they are assembled.

questions.explanation: The period-length relation, thermal expansion, and two compensations build the paragraph. The keyed choice matches the passage's actual movement and purpose, while the other options describe content or functions the text does not contain.

distractor_rationales.C: No invention narrative appears.
distractor_rationales.B: Temperature is the complication.
distractor_rationales.D: No assembly order is given.

questions.stimulus: A farmer plants a cover crop after harvest. The roots hold soil through winter rains, and the plants add organic matter when they are turned in. The field looks idle, but the cover crop is working. Yield in the following season often rises even though nothing was harvested in between.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To explain the unseen benefits of a crop grown between harvests.
To describe how to harvest a cover crop for profit.
To argue that bare soil is better for yields.

questions.explanation: The passage explains what the cover crop does while looking idle.

distractor_rationales.B: Nothing is harvested from the cover crop.
distractor_rationales.D: Bare soil is the contrast case.
distractor_rationales.C: No brands are compared.

questions.stimulus: The first tests of a new vaccine measure immune response, not protection. A later trial follows thousands of people to see who becomes ill. The two stages answer different questions, and a strong immune response in the first does not guarantee success in the second. Reading the first result as a verdict is a common error.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It reports the results of a completed field trial.
It distinguishes two stages, explains what each measures, and warns against conflating them.
It argues that early trials are unnecessary.
It describes the manufacturing process of a vaccine.

questions.explanation: The paragraph separates the two questions and names the mistake of merging them.

distractor_rationales.D: Manufacturing is not described.
distractor_rationales.C: Early trials are presented as one stage.
distractor_rationales.A: No results are reported.

questions.stimulus: A stone arch bridge carries load by compression. Each block pushes against its neighbors, and the curve directs the force into the abutments. The bridge can stand for centuries because the material is strong in compression. It fails when water scours the foundation and the abutments move, not because the stone crumbles.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It compares stone and steel bridges and prefers steel.
It argues that arches carry load in tension.
It explains the structural principle and then names the usual cause of failure.
It describes the construction sequence of a bridge.

questions.explanation: The principle of compression is followed by scour as the failure mode.

distractor_rationales.A: No steel comparison appears.
distractor_rationales.D: Construction order is not given.
distractor_rationales.B: The passage specifies compression.

questions.stimulus: An archive received a box of letters with no catalog. A conservator noted the paper, ink and postmarks before anyone read them. The postmarks placed the letters in three decades; the ink identified two writers. Reading came last, after the physical evidence had narrowed the possibilities.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes how paper is manufactured.
It argues that letters should be read before being examined.
It lists the contents of the box in detail.
It narrates a sequence in which physical analysis precedes reading.

questions.explanation: The order of steps is the structure the question asks about.

distractor_rationales.B: Reading comes last in the passage.
distractor_rationales.C: Contents are summarized, not listed.
distractor_rationales.A: Manufacture is not discussed.

questions.stimulus: A tidal flat looks uniform from a distance. Up close it holds channels, pools and patches of mud of different grain sizes. Each patch drains at a different rate, so the animals living in them experience different periods of exposure. A single square meter can contain several distinct habitats.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the purpose of the text?

choices.text: To list the species found on tidal flats.
To show how small-scale variation creates distinct habitats on a seemingly uniform flat.
To describe the tides that cover a flat twice a day.
To argue that grain size has no effect on drainage.

questions.explanation: The contrast between distant and close views carries the point.

distractor_rationales.C: Tide timing is not the subject.
distractor_rationales.D: Grain size is tied to drainage.
distractor_rationales.A: Species are mentioned generally.

questions.stimulus: A baker's starter failed after a move to a new city. The flour was different, and so was the water. Replacing the flour restored the rise within a week, which suggested that the water was not the problem. The starter had been selective about its food all along.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It describes a problem, tests one cause, and draws a conclusion from the result.
It compares two cities and their baking traditions.
It argues that water quality never affects baking.
It lists the steps for making a starter from scratch.

questions.explanation: The flour swap isolates the cause and produces the conclusion.

distractor_rationales.B: No traditions are compared.
distractor_rationales.C: Water is ruled out only after the flour test.
distractor_rationales.D: No recipe is given.

questions.stimulus: A lighthouse's beam is narrow because a wide beam spreads its light too thin to be seen far. Rotating the beam sweeps the horizon, so a distant ship sees a flash rather than a steady glow. The flash pattern identifies the lighthouse, which is why each station has a different interval.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that a wide beam is easier to see at sea.
It explains a design choice, describes its effect, and states a further function of that effect.
It narrates the construction of a lighthouse tower.
It compares two lighthouses of different heights.

questions.explanation: Narrow beam, rotation and identifying flash build on one another.

questions.stimulus: The curator's notes were so ______ that even a reader unfamiliar with the period could follow the argument.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'even a reader unfamiliar with the period could follow' names the quality the notes need: clarity. 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand, so it is the only choice that explains why an outsider could follow the argument.

distractor_rationales.C: 'Terse' means brief to the point of abruptness, which would not help an unfamiliar reader follow anything.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Ornate' means heavily decorated, the opposite of the plain clarity the sentence praises.
distractor_rationales.B: 'Tentative' means uncertain, and hesitant notes would not make an argument easy to follow.

questions.stimulus: The dispute over water rights proved ______: three mediators resigned, and neither side would agree even to the wording of a meeting notice.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The evidence is cumulative failure: mediators quit and the parties cannot agree even on a meeting notice. 'Intractable' means stubbornly difficult to control or solve, which matches a dispute that defeats every attempt at settlement.

distractor_rationales.D: 'Brittle' describes something that breaks easily, not a dispute that resists every attempt at settlement.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Generous' is the opposite of what the resigned mediators and the stalled notice show.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Transient' means short-lived, but the sentence describes a conflict stubborn enough to outlast three mediators.

questions.stimulus: Though the expedition is remembered for its drama, its daily log was ______, recording little more than mileage, weather and the state of the mules.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The contrast with the expedition's dramatic reputation sets up an ordinary record. 'Prosaic' means dull and matter-of-fact, exactly what a log of mileage, weather and mule condition is.

distractor_rationales.B: 'Lyrical' suggests expressive, songlike writing, but the log records only mileage, weather and mules.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Perilous' would describe danger, and the sentence lists ordinary bookkeeping instead.
distractor_rationales.D: 'Cryptic' means deliberately mysterious, while the entries named are plain and easy to read.

questions.stimulus: The trial's results were ______: the treatment helped patients over sixty but showed no measurable effect on younger ones.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: A result that helps one group and does not help another cannot be read as a single verdict. 'Equivocal' means open to more than one interpretation, which is precisely the divided outcome described.

distractor_rationales.A: 'Conclusive' would settle the question, yet the results point in two directions.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Negligible' would mean the treatment did almost nothing, ignoring the benefit seen in older patients.
distractor_rationales.B: 'Unanimous' describes agreement among people, not a split pattern of results.

questions.stimulus: The committee adopted a ______ schedule, one it would replace once the survey of the new site was complete.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The clause 'one it would replace once the survey was complete' defines the schedule as a stand-in. 'Provisional' means arranged for the present and likely to change, which is exactly that arrangement.

distractor_rationales.C: 'Permanent' contradicts the plan to replace the schedule later.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Meticulous' praises care in detail, but the sentence is about the schedule's temporary status.
distractor_rationales.B: 'Punitive' would mean designed as a punishment, which nothing in the sentence suggests.

questions.stimulus: In a report crowded with technical detail, the most ______ finding was that the bridge's expansion joints had been sealed shut.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The sentence picks one finding out of many because it matters most. 'Salient' means most noticeable or important, which fits a safety-relevant detail standing out from technical clutter.

distractor_rationales.B: 'Negligible' means too small to matter, the reverse of a finding singled out from a crowded report.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Oblique' means indirect, but a sealed joint is a direct and concrete fact.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Ornamental' describes decoration, not a structural fault worth noticing.

questions.stimulus: The link between the two sightings was ______, resting on a single blurry photograph and the memory of one retired ranger.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The evidence is deliberately described as slight: a blurry photograph and a single recollection. 'Tenuous' means weak or flimsy, which matches a connection that barely holds.

distractor_rationales.D: 'Robust' means strong and dependable, the opposite of a case built on one photograph and one memory.
distractor_rationales.B: 'Explicit' means stated clearly, but the problem is the thinness of the evidence, not its clarity.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Reciprocal' describes something mutual, which the sentence never claims.

questions.stimulus: The monastery's ______ cells contained a narrow bed, a stool and nothing else.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: A room with a bed, a stool and nothing else is defined by severe simplicity. 'Austere' means plain and without comfort or ornament, which is exactly the cell described.

distractor_rationales.C: 'Lavish' means rich and abundant, the opposite of a bed, a stool and nothing else.
distractor_rationales.D: 'Cluttered' would mean filled with many objects, but the cell holds two.
distractor_rationales.B: 'Provisional' means temporary, which the sentence does not suggest.

questions.stimulus: A ______ correspondent, she could fill a half-hour interview with anecdotes and never once repeat herself.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Filling thirty minutes with anecdotes and never repeating herself is fluent, abundant speech. 'Voluble' means speaking readily and at length, which is the only choice consistent with that performance.

distractor_rationales.D: 'Reticent' means unwilling to speak freely, which contradicts filling a half-hour interview.
distractor_rationales.B: 'Laconic' means using very few words, the opposite of a stream of anecdotes.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Taciturn' means habitually silent, again the reverse of the behaviour described.

questions.stimulus: The editor's ______ cuts removed three redundant scenes without touching a single line the author considered essential.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The editor removed what was redundant and preserved what mattered, which is careful judgment. 'Judicious' means showing good sense, precisely the quality of cuts that are both effective and respectful of the text.

distractor_rationales.A: 'Arbitrary' means done without reason, but the cuts are explained by redundancy.
distractor_rationales.D: 'Lavish' means abundant or extravagant, not selective and careful.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Hasty' means too quick, while the sentence describes precision in sparing essential lines.

questions.stimulus: Critics called the score ______, noting that its main theme repeated a folk melody the composer had used in two earlier works.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The evidence is reuse: the main theme repeats a melody heard twice before. 'Derivative' means imitative of an earlier source rather than original, which is exactly the criticism the reviewers made.

distractor_rationales.A: 'Innovative' means introducing something new, but the theme is borrowed from the composer's own earlier works.
distractor_rationales.D: 'Spare' describes thin texture, which the sentence never mentions.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Dissonant' describes harsh harmony, also absent from the sentence.

questions.stimulus: The sensor's ______ readings puzzled the technicians: every other gauge on the site agreed with the forecast.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: One sensor disagrees with every other gauge and with the forecast, so its readings are the exception. 'Anomalous' means deviating from what is standard or expected, which explains the puzzlement.

distractor_rationales.C: 'Consistent' would mean the readings matched the others, which is what puzzled the technicians.
distractor_rationales.D: 'Calibrated' describes an instrument that has been adjusted correctly, not a reading that departs from every gauge.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Marginal' means slight, but the contrast is between one dissenting sensor and every other gauge.

questions.stimulus: Through ______ record-keeping, the archivist tracked every loan, repair and misfiling across four decades.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Keeping a complete record of every loan, repair and misfiling over forty years takes steady, painstaking attention. 'Assiduous' means showing great care and perseverance, which matches that sustained effort.

distractor_rationales.D: 'Sporadic' means occurring at irregular intervals, which could not produce a four-decade record.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Reluctant' describes unwillingness, not the diligence implied by tracking every transaction.
distractor_rationales.B: 'Cursory' means hurried and superficial, the opposite of tracking every loan and repair.

questions.stimulus: The citation turned out to be ______: the article it named had never been published, and its author did not exist.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: A source that was never published and an author who never existed make the citation false rather than merely unfamiliar. 'Spurious' means not genuine or valid, which fits a fabricated reference.

distractor_rationales.C: 'Obscure' means little known, but the citation names an article that never existed at all.
distractor_rationales.B: 'Seminal' means highly influential, which a nonexistent article cannot be.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Verbatim' means word for word, a description of quotation rather than of a fabricated source.

questions.stimulus: The model is appealingly ______, predicting the entire outcome from just two measured variables.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: A model that predicts everything from two variables is economical in its assumptions. 'Parsimonious' means unusually frugal or economical, and in this context it praises a simple explanation that accounts for a great deal.

distractor_rationales.B: 'Elaborate' means having many parts, the opposite of a model built on two variables.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Opaque' means hard to understand, but the sentence praises the model as appealing.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Redundant' means needlessly repetitive, which a two-variable model is not.

questions.stimulus: The board was ______ that the deadline would not move, despite three requests for an extension.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Three requests for an extension were turned aside, which shows a fixed position. 'Adamant' means refusing to be persuaded, exactly the stance described.

distractor_rationales.D: 'Ambivalent' means having mixed feelings, which would not explain a refusal to move the deadline.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Amenable' means open to suggestion, the opposite of resisting three requests.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Indifferent' suggests the board did not care, yet it repeatedly refused to change the date.

questions.stimulus: The desert bloom is ______, lasting sometimes only a single morning before the heat closes the petals.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The flower exists for a morning and then closes. 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time, which is the defining fact the sentence gives.

distractor_rationales.D: 'Hardy' means able to survive harsh conditions, while the bloom collapses in a morning.
distractor_rationales.A: 'Perennial' means lasting year after year, the opposite of a single morning.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Dormant' means temporarily inactive, not briefly alive and then gone.

questions.stimulus: The ______ design survived two winters of heavy snow and a summer of record heat without a single repair.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The design endured extreme weather with no repairs, which is a test of strength and resilience. 'Robust' means sturdy and able to withstand adverse conditions, exactly the performance described.

distractor_rationales.B: 'Fragile' means easily broken, which two winters and a summer without repair rule out.
distractor_rationales.C: 'Ornate' concerns decoration, not the ability to endure weather.
distractor_rationales.D: 'Rigid' means stiff and unyielding, which is not what the sentence's evidence establishes.

questions.stimulus: Pressed by reporters, the spokesperson ______, praising the proposal's goals while declining to say whether the agency supported it.
